# Finding the Number of Banach Spaces on $\mathbb{R}$

## Setting Up the Problem

A Banach space is a **complete** normed vector space. I need to determine how many Banach space structures can be placed on the set $\mathbb{R}$ with its standard vector space structure (1-dimensional over $\mathbb{R}$).

## Classifying All Norms on 1-Dimensional $\mathbb{R}$

Let $\|\cdot\|$ be any norm on $\mathbb{R}$. By the homogeneity property of norms:

$$\|x\| = \|x \cdot 1\| = |x| \cdot \|1\|$$

Letting $c = \|1\| > 0$ (by positive definiteness), every norm on $\mathbb{R}$ must be of the form:
$$\|x\| = c|x|, \quad c > 0$$

## Verifying Completeness

For any $c > 0$, a sequence $(x_n)$ is Cauchy in $\|\cdot\|$ iff:
$$c|x_n - x_m| \to 0 \iff |x_n - x_m| \to 0$$

Since $\mathbb{R}$ is complete under the standard absolute value metric, every Cauchy sequence converges in $\mathbb{R}$. Therefore, **every** norm $\|x\| = c|x|$ makes $(\mathbb{R}, \|\cdot\|)$ a Banach space.

## Counting Distinct Banach Spaces

While there are uncountably many norms (one for each $c > 0$), all norms $\|x\| = c|x|$ define **isometrically isomorphic** Banach spaces. The map $T: (\mathbb{R}, |\cdot|) \to (\mathbb{R}, c|\cdot|)$ given by $T(x) = c \cdot x$ (or equivalently, scaling) is a linear isometry between any two such structures.

Since a "Banach space" as a mathematical structure is determined up to canonical isomorphism, all choices of $c > 0$ yield the **same** Banach space structure on $\mathbb{R}$.

## Conclusion

There is exactly **one** Banach space structure on $\mathbb{R}$ (the standard one-dimensional real Banach space). All valid norms are equivalent and produce isomorphic complete normed spaces.

$$\boxed{1}$$
